# Your Turn {background-color="#006666"}

- Check how many cores the machine you are using has `parallel::detectCores()`

- Initialize a cluster with fewer than the number of cores available

- Run the R code below on your machine 

- Parallelize the statement, re-run it and time 

```{r message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
library(nycflights13)
library(dplyr)

system.time(
delays <- flights |> group_by(flight) |>
  summarize(
    mean_delay = mean(arr_delay, na.rm=FALSE)
  ) 
)
```

# `multidplyr`

```{r}
library(multidplyr)

cl <- new_cluster(8)
cluster_library(cl, "dplyr")
```

# Send data to nodes

If the data is loaded in the main session, create partition; then work like normal

```{r}
library(nycflights13)

flight_dest <- flights %>% group_by(dest) %>% partition(cl)
flight_dest
```



# `collect()` results

```{r}
flight_dest %>% 
  summarise(delay = mean(dep_delay, na.rm = TRUE), n = n()) %>% 
  collect()
```

# Your Turn {background-color="#006666"}

`set.seed` allows you to set the seed before using a random number generator
to create reproducible samples. 

```{r}
set.seed(123)
runif(3)
set.seed(123)
runif(3)
```

How would this work for a parallel process?
What else do we need to ensure?

# Random Number Generation

```{r}
library(parallel)
set.seed(123)

mclapply(c(5,5), runif, mc.cores=2)
```
How do we ensure reproducibility and independence?

# RNG in Parallel

`clusterSetRNGStream` uses RNG "L'Ecuyer-CMRG" that produces _streams_ of independent random numbers

```{r}
cl <- makeCluster(4)

clusterSetRNGStream(cl, 123)

results <- parLapply(cl, 1:4, function(i) {
  data.frame(i, runif=runif(5))
}) |> data.frame()

clusterSetRNGStream(cl, 123)

results2 <- parLapply(cl, 1:4,  function(i) {
  data.frame(i, runif=runif(5))
}) |> data.frame()

identical(results, results2)
stopCluster(cl)
```

# 

```{r}
results
```

# When NOT to Parallelize

- Small tasks
- Fast vectorized code
- Memory limits
